title: Universal Parent Hamiltonians for Adiabatic Warm Starts
abstract: Computing the ground state properties of quantum systems is an important potential application of quantum computing. The success probability of quantum phase estimation approaches to ground state problems is proportional to the overlap of the input state with the ground state. Local ansatz state approaches suffer from the orthogonality catastrophe, whereas adiabatic state preparation (ASP) can prepare good approximations with a cost growing with the inverse square of the minimum spectral gap along the adiabatic path. When the initial and target Hamiltonians lie in quantum phases separated by a first order phase transition, the minimum spectral gap along the adiabatic path becomes exponentially small as a function of system size. We pursue a solution to this problem based on choosing an initial Hamiltonian for adiabatic state preparation whose ground state lies in the same quantum phase as the target ground state. We develop a protocol for universal adiabatic warm starts with universal parent Hamiltonians (UPHAWS) that can initialize ASP in any state whose preparation circuit is known. We use the Feynman--Kitaev clock Hamiltonian as a universal parent Hamiltonian, for preparation circuits with and without mid circuit measurement. We benchmark the framework on a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric matrix product state (MPS) family interpolating to a target GHZ Hamiltonian, and on the linear $H_6$ chain under symmetric bond stretching. For the $H_6$ system a bond-dimension-$4$ matrix product state warm-start increases the minimum gap on the adiabatic path by a factor of two relative to the Hartree-Fock initialization. To perform these classical benchmark simulations we develop a momentum-space truncation of the adiabatic Hamiltonian that may be of independent interest.
summary: This paper introduces the Universal Parent Hamiltonian Adiabatic Warm Start (UPHAWS) protocol to solve the problem of initializing quantum simulations near quantum phase transitions. By selecting an initial Hamiltonian whose ground state shares the target's quantum phase, it prevents the minimum spectral gap from collapsing exponentially with system size. This significantly improves the feasibility and scaling of adiabatic state preparation for complex many-body systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is efficiently preparing an initial quantum state with high overlap to accurately estimate the ground state properties of a target Hamiltonian using Quantum Phase Estimation (QPE).
main_result: The authors propose Universal Parent Hamiltonians for Adiabatic Warm Starts (UPHAWS), demonstrating that initializing adiabatic state preparation with a parent Hamiltonian whose ground state is in the same quantum phase as the target can significantly improve the minimum spectral gap.
method: The work develops a theoretical protocol using 'parent Hamiltonians' and analyzes the required time scaling ($T \propto 1/\Delta^2$) for Adiabatic State Preparation (ASP) across quantum phase transitions.
model_or_system: The framework is tested on general quantum systems, specifically benchmarking against an MPS family interpolating to a GHZ Hamiltonian and the linear H6 chain undergoing bond stretching.
key_observables: Minimum spectral gap ($\Delta$), Adiabatic fidelity ($F(t)$), and the initial state overlap $\langle \Upsilon_0|\Psi_0angle$.
important_parameters: The system size (N) and the separation between quantum phases, which dictates whether the minimum gap shrinks exponentially.
main_assumptions: It is assumed that choosing an initial Hamiltonian whose ground state resides in the same quantum phase as the target allows for efficient warm-starting of ASP.
figures_summary: The figures compare the minimum rescaled adiabatic gap for different initialization geometries (e.g., localized vs. delocalized starts) across bond stretching, showing that appropriate initial states maintain a large gap where others collapse near phase boundaries.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of state preparation bottlenecks in QPE, introduces the UPHAWS protocol using parent Hamiltonians like the Feynman–Kitaev clock Hamiltonian, and validates this approach through detailed benchmarks on specific physical models (MPS/H6 chain).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses resource estimation for quantum computation by providing a concrete method to circumvent spectral gap closing issues inherent in adiabatic state preparation when crossing phase boundaries.
